Not the most stylish IMO but you can't go wrong with a glock, such an excellent and reliable firearm.

Home defense get a shotgun or a ar-15. ccw get something compact or subcompact with at least 10 round mag in 9mm or 45acp.

Look on the internet at gun ranges in your area, lots have try before you buy deals, or at least go try a couple to see what fits you and what you can shoot best with. I would also suggest taking some form of a safety course and familiarizing yourself with the different types of guns, how they operate, how to take them apart, and how to clean them.

Edit : I may have misread your post, if the gun is for a 83 year old women get her a snub nose revolver chambered in .38. Semi auto pistols will be hard for her to rack and handle. A revolver will always fire and is very easy to use.

The best gun is the one that she will always carry, and one that is comfortable and convenient enough for her to use at a moment's notice. I know this is not quite the answer you were looking for (make/model), but I believe it's the best answer anyone can give.

She needs to feel comfortable with its use, and it should feel ergonomically suitable in her hand. It should be any reasonable cartridge in terms of stopping power. I don't want to start a debate on calibers and ft/lbs, but a 9mm in my opinion is sufficient for self defense and easily managed, even for an elderly person.

I suggest taking her to a gun store to hold many guns to let her see what gun naturally aims in her hand well and what feels simple for her to use, while being convenient for carry in whatever way she prefers. If possible go to a range that allows her to fire many guns to see what she thinks of each, and go from there.
